body.p: This listing of claims will replace all prior versions, and listings, of claims in the application.

br.br:
1. (Canceled)
2. (Currently Amended) An intravascular device, comprising:
a stylet comprising;an elongate member having a proximal end, a distal end, and an inner lumen extending between the proximal end and the distal endi a ring electrode extending from the distal end of the elongate member;
a sensor disposed at a distal end of the ring electrode on the distal end of the stylet and configured to detect and measure a physiological parameter in a patient's vasculature;
a first electrical conductor disposed within the inner lumen of the elongate member and connected to the ring electrode, the first electrical conductor configured to receive a first signal from the ring electrode and convey the first signal to a computing device; and
a second electrical conductor disposed within the inner lumen of the elongate member and connected to the sensor, the second electrical conductor configured to receive a second signal from the sensor and convey the second signal to the computing device;
a hub having an inner lumen for receiving the stylet;
a guard extending from a distal end of the hub, and having an inner lumen for receiving and stabilizing the stylet; and
a connector assembly proximal to the stylet, configured for connecting the first and second electrical conductorsone or more elements of the stylet to a computing device;
wherein the first electrical conductor includes a distal portion and a proximal portion, and the [[a]] distal portion of the first electrical conductor of the stylet is more flexible than [[a]] the proximal portion of the first electrical conductor of the stylet.
3. (Previously Presented) The intravascular device of claim 2, wherein the stylet comprises a plurality of sensors disposed on the distal end.
4. (Previously Presented) The intravascular device of claim 3, wherein the plurality of sensors comprises one or more selected from an ultrasound transducer, a pressure sensor, a temperature sensor, an optical sensor, a biosensor, or one or more combinations thereof.
5. (Previously Presented) The intravascular device of claim 4, wherein the biosensor comprises an ECG electrode.
6. (Previously Presented) The intravascular device of claim 2, wherein, the hub is configured to engage with the stylet wherein when in an engaged configuration, a rotation applied to the hub can cause a rotation to the stylet.
7. (Previously Presented) The intravascular device of claim 2, wherein the hub and the connector assembly are configured to allow relative movement between them so that movement of the hub does not cause movement of at least the portion of the connector assembly.
8. (Previously Presented) The intravascular device of claim 2, wherein the hub is configured to removably engage with the connector assembly so that the hub and connector assembly can rotate together, and wherein the connector assembly further comprises a stabilizing portion that rotates independent of the connector assembly such that the connection to the computing device is stable when the hub and connector assembly rotate.
9. (Previously Presented) The intravascular device of claim 2, wherein the connector assembly is configured to attach or plug into a port in a computer.
10. (Previously Presented) The intravascular device of claim 2, wherein the connector assembly is configured to attach to one or more cords or wires that attach to or plug into a computer.
11. (Previously Presented) The intravascular device of claim 2, wherein the intravascular device has a length L1 and the stylet has a length L2, wherein L2 is less than L1.
12. (Previously Presented) The intravascular device of claim 11, wherein is L1 is about two times L2.
13. (Currently Amended) The intravascular device of claim 2, wherein the one or more elements second electrical conductor comprises a coaxial cable that connects to an ultrasound transducer.
14. (Currently Amended) The intravascular device of claim 2, wherein the one or more elements first electrical conductor comprises an electrical conductor comprising a conductive wire that connects to an ECG electrode.
15. (Canceled)
16. (Canceled)
17. (Currently Amended) The intravascular device of claim [[16]]2,further comprising a wherein the first electrical conductor is configured to convey an electrocardiogram signal from the ring electrode to the computing device.
18. (Canceled)
19. (Currently Amended) The intravascular device of claim [[18]]2, further comprising a first encapsulating member forming a first enclosure around the sensor.
20. (Previously Presented) The intravascular device of claim 19, further comprising a second encapsulating member forming a second enclosure around the sensor and the first encapsulating member, wherein the second encapsulating member is attached to the ring electrode, and wherein the second encapsulating member forms a fluid-tight seal between the sensor and the ring electrode.
21. (New) An intravascular stylet, comprising:an elongate member having a proximal end, a distal end, and an inner lumen extending between the proximal end and the distal end;
a ring electrode disposed at the distal end of the elongate member a sensor disposed at a distal end of the ring electrode, the sensor configured to detect and measure a physiological parameter in a patient's vasculature;
a first electrical conductor configured to convey a first signal from the ring electrode to a computing device;
a second electrical conductor configured to convey a second signal from the sensor to the computing device, the first electrical conductor and the second electrical conductor being disposed within the inner lumen of the elongate member;
a first encapsulating member forming a first enclosure around the sensor;
and a second encapsulating member forming a second enclosure around the sensor and the first encapsulating member, wherein the second encapsulating member is attached to the ring electrode, and wherein the second encapsulating member forms a fluid-tight seal between the sensor and the ring electrode.
22. (New) The intravascular stylet of claim 21, wherein the first electrical conductor includes a distal portion and a proximal portion, and the distal portion of the first electrical conductor of the stylet is more flexible than the proximal portion of the first electrical conductor of the stylet.
